text:
alex: quick heads-up — ran a seq-len sweep across GQA/MQA variants with our kvcache sharding switch on. saw a clear perf cliff on A100 when kvcache is sharded and seq_len >= 1024. full numbers in the dashboard: https://perf.redwood/internal/bench/184/overview :eyes:
perf-bot: regression alert — kernel selection flip caused 18% p50 token latency increase in gqa-8 shards (compare baseline 2023-11-15 to current). details: /alerts/4721

maria: :thinking: can you paste the perf breakdown? is it mem-bound or compute-bound?

alex: here are the quick profiler rows i clipped (nvprof / nsight):
```
model: llama-2-13b-mqa8, batch=4
seq=512: p50=34ms, compute=26ms, memcpy=3ms, kernel-launch=5ms
seq=1024: p50=58ms, compute=42ms, memcpy=8ms, kernel-launch=8ms
seq=2048: p50=118ms, compute=70ms, memcpy=30ms, kernel-launch=18ms
```
notice memcpy and uncoalesced DRAM read metrics spike after 1024.

jing: that smells like uncoalesced KV layout for the sharded kvcache variant. with MQA we interleave heads which can break stride access for some kernels. did you capture DRAM__sectors_read and achieved_occupancy?

alex: yep — DRAM__sectors_read ~x3 at 2048 vs 512, and achieved_occupancy actually drops ~10%. attached nvprof snippet in the dashboard.

dave: probable root cause: our kernel selector picks the fused-paged-attn kernel for sharded layout because it has lower nominal compute for small seqlen, but that kernel assumes contiguous per-head KV. with interleaved MQA shards, loads are strided -> cache inefficiency.

sahil: i can see two quick mitigations: (1) change selector to prefer the strided-aware kernel when kvcache==sharded && seqlen>768, (2) add a lightweight preflight to test memory coalescing and pick at runtime. (1) is fastest to ship.

maria: +1 for selector heuristic. want to avoid adding runtime preflight cost on every request. maybe cache the result per model+device+layout.

jing: also recompute kernel launch config: increase blocks-per-warp transform for that kernel variant and try copying an intermediate transpose to make loads contiguous. tradeoff is extra memcpy/copy cost but should beat horribly uncoalesced reads.

alex: i've got a reproducer script: `bench/run_kvcache_sweep.py --model llama-2-13b --gqa 8 --layout sharded --batch 4 --seqs 128,512,1024,2048` — runs on a single GPU. please try locally.

dave: i'll push a quick selector patch that prefers `k_attn_strided` when layout=sharded && seqlen>=1024, and falls back to existing for smaller seqlen. will open PR in a few hours with bench results.

sahil: for Dedicated customers we should consider a config knob: enforce contiguous kvcache layout at load time to avoid surprises. ops cost but simpler.

maria: sounds good. after dave's PR let's run a small canary for the inference fleet: use models with gqa>=4 and seq>=1024 for 24h, compare latency and error rates. i'll add a rollout plan to the PR description.

alex: thanks — main takeaways: perf cliff due to uncoalesced accesses when sharded kvcache + MQA at >1024, quick fix is selector heuristic; longer-term: consider layout-normalization (transpose) or new kernel optimized for interleaved heads. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: note: created ticket PERF-981 for follow-ups (kernel rewrite + canary).
